about.about_text: The Latin American Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (CLIHC) is managed by the SIGCHI Latin American HCI Community (LAIHC). CLIHC is a premier conference that brings together the Latin American and international HCI research communities to discuss and exchange ideas, methods, approaches, and techniques for designing interactive user experiences and encourages intercultural exchange and cooperation between people with different backgrounds and needs. This conference has its origin in Rio de Janeiro 2003 (Brazil), following editions in Cuernavaca 2005 (Mexico), Rio de Janeiro 2007 (Brazil), Merida 2009 (Mexico), Porto de Galinhas 2011 (Brazil), Guanacaste 2013 (Costa Rica), Córdoba 2015 (Argentina), Antigua 2017 (Guatemala), Panama City 2019 (Panama), Virtual Conference 2021 (Online), and Puebla 2023 (México).

organizers.title: Organizers
organizers.intro: The primary objective of the 2026 Latin American Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (CLIHC) is to foster collaboration, discussion, and knowledge exchange among international and Latin American HCI researchers. The conference aims to promote human-centered and culturally aware artificial intelligence design and development, and provide a platform for the presentation and discussion of new ideas, methods, and techniques for designing interactive user experiences. The conference will be held in Puebla, Mexico, and is organized by a diverse group of experts from Latin America and beyond.

papers.introduction_p1: The XII Latin American Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (CLIHC 2026), aims to provide a premier forum that brings together the Latin American and international Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) research communities to discuss and share ideas, methods, approaches, and techniques for designing, implementing, and evaluating interactive user experiences. In accordance with previous editions, we believe that HCI must foster the production of technology that can be used by and benefit as many people as possible, enabling intercultural exchange and cooperation between people with different backgrounds and needs.
papers.introduction_p2: This year, CLIHC 2026 will take place in two cities, Aracaju/Brazil and Oaxaca/Mexico. However, the presentation of the full papers will only take place in the satellite city of Aracaju, Brazil. For now, is open to submissions in the following category:
papers.introduction_p3: Authors are invited to prepare and submit papers reporting on research projects, innovative designs, user studies, models of interaction, field studies, case studies, and others. Academics, researchers, practitioners and professionals from industry, as well as undergraduate and graduate students are welcome to participate in the peer-reviewed selection of the works that will be presented at the conference, from May 06 to 08, 2026.
papers.topics_title: Topics of submissions may cover all aspects of HCI, including, but not limited to:
papers.topic_9: HCI and Artificial Intelligence (e.g, Human-Centered AI and Interaction Design; Human-AI Interaction; HCI in AI-Powered Systems; User Experience and Design for AI Systems; Responsible and Ethical HCI for AI Applications; eXplainable Artificial Intelligence - XAI)
papers.submission_dates_p1: All manuscripts must be submitted fully anonymized. Please consider an international audience: e.g., avoid local terms, and use the international system of units. In addition, consider following accessibility guidelines (CLIHC 2023 edition, opens in a new tab).
papers.deadlines_aoe: Deadlines are at midnight AoE (Anywhere on Earth).
papers.ethics_code_p1: We abide by the ACM Code of Ethics. We expect that all submissions, underlying research, and behavior during the review process and conference comply with the principles and responsibilities outlined by the code.
papers.submission_process_p1: Full paper submissions are to be made through JEMS3 System (Journal and Event Management System): https://jems3.sbc.org.br/events/510
papers.submission_process_p2: Submission format to be used for each category will follow the Brazilian Computer Society template. Authors may choose to work in one of the following formats:
papers.full_papers_p1: Research projects that have achieved a mature stage and present an original contribution to the state of the art are welcome to submit in the full paper category. Submissions must be relevant to the subject of the conference, and may not have been published nor be under review in any other conference or journal. The maximum length for full papers is 15 pages including references, and papers must be written in English, Portuguese, or Spanish.
papers.full_papers_p2: The papers will be reviewed by at least two reviewers in a double-anonymous process. Please note that submitted papers must be anonymized, including references to the authors’ own previous work.
papers.full_papers_p3: We are working to ensure that accepted papers will be published in the SBC OpenLib (SOL) (a digital library maintained by the Brazilian Computer Society - SBC). In addition, best papers will be recommended for submitting an extended version and be published in a special edition that we are negotiating with a prestigious HCI or Computer Science journal.
